comments.content: `latestVersion` is nullable and is `null` in the very case this fix is meant to cover: `InstallationManagerImpl.saveNewInstalledApp()` persists `latestVersion = null` on a fresh install (and `clearUpdateMetadata()` nulls it as well). So a user who installs the newest release and immediately rolls back to an older build before any periodic check runs won't get any skip tag, and the next check will re-offer the release they deliberately regressed from. Consider falling back to the version being rolled back from (`installedApp.installedVersion`) or the newest known release tag.

comments.content: The skip is persisted *before* the install runs, but the install path immediately overwrites the effect of this write. Once the downgraded APK is installed, `saveInstalledAppToDatabase(isUpdate = true)` → `InstalledAppsRepositoryImpl.updateAppVersion()` recomputes `isUpdateAvailable = VersionMath.isVersionNewer(snapshotLatestVersion, newTag)` and ignores `skippedReleaseTag`. In exactly the scenario this block targets (installed tag V8, `latestVersion` V10) that evaluates to `true`, so `isUpdateAvailable` is flipped back to `1` in the DB right after the install. The details screen observes `installedApp` from that DB row (see `observeInstalledApp` → `SmartInstallButton`), and the apps list also reads `isUpdateAvailable`, so the "Update to v10" CTA / update badge reappears for the release the user just skipped. The suppression only returns after the next periodic `checkForUpdates`, which sees `matchesSkipped` and writes `isUpdateAvailable = 0`. Suggestion: apply the skip after the install settles (e.g. in the `OrchestratorStage.Completed` branch) or re-run `installedAppsRepository.checkForUpdates(packageName)` once the install completes, so `updateAppVersion` cannot undo it.
